limiting_points.suggested_action: Frame the advance as an integrated platform and distinguish it from the component strategies described in the background.
limiting_points.text: The contribution is system-level: the manuscript combines established CRISPR delivery, metal-ion/ROS biology, and STING-priming concepts into PMZH rather than presenting each component as a new mechanism.

supporting_points.suggested_action: Retain the integrated-delivery and dual-mechanism framing in the contribution statement.
supporting_points.text: The reported contribution integrates SLC43A2-targeting CRISPR/Cas9 delivery with Mn/Zn-MOF-mediated ROS and cGAS/STING activation, then follows that design through editing and pathway readouts.

strengths.suggested_action: Preserve the linked delivery, editing, and T-cell evidence sequence when presenting the mechanism.
strengths.text: The evidence sequence connects carrier uptake and plasmid delivery to SLC43A2 editing, methionine-related T-cell readouts, and in-vivo tumor-cell and infiltrating-CD8+ T-cell measurements.

strengths.suggested_action: Keep the cellular, dendritic-cell, and animal-model readouts clearly separated while showing their mechanistic connection.
strengths.text: The final study spans tumor-cell STING-associated readouts, BMDC measurements, and in-vivo antitumor and immune-cell analyses rather than relying on a single efficacy endpoint.

summary.text: The paper reports PMZH, an HA-coated Mn/Zn metal-organic framework that encapsulates a CRISPR/Cas9 plasmid targeting SLC43A2. It links SLC43A2 disruption and altered methionine competition to T-cell readouts, while Mn/Zn-associated ROS, mtDNA release, and STING-associated signaling are measured in cells and BMDCs. The in-vivo work evaluates tumor growth, immune-cell infiltration, distant-tumor control, and a lung-metastasis model in preclinical mouse systems.
